To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

higher levels of markers of macrophage and microglial activation, and axonal injury, in plasma and cere-spinal fluid, were associated with prospective memory, but not retrospective memory, in HIV-1 infection, suggesting a dissociation between the two memory domains.

higher levels of MCP1 in plasma and soluble receptor for TNF type II and tau were associated with Pro-M but not RM, and markers of astrocytogenesis, growth factor depletion and HIV-1 viral replication did not predict Pro-M or RM.

higher plasma monocyte chemo-attractant protein- 1 (MCP1) and cerebrospin-al fluid tau and soluble tumor necrosis factor receptor II (sTNFR2) were associated with impaired prospective memory (Pro M), but not retrospective memory (RM), in HIV-1 infection, suggesting that ProM impairment is associated with specific mechanisms of macrophages and axonal injury, but not astrocytosis and growth factor depletion, in this disorder.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the neuropathophysiology underlying the impairment of prospective memory in HIV-1.
the neurobiological underpinnings of prospective memory (memory for future intentions) in persons with HIV infection.
the neurocognitive and neurobehavioral consequences of HIV-1 infection in the context of the AIDS pandemic.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HIV infection and AIDS are not a disease of the brain, but a disease of the immune system that has a profound effect on the brain.
the HIV-1 disease is associated with ProM impairment, but the underlying pathophysiology of this impairment is not yet known.
the HIV-1 infection is associated with impaired prospective memory, which is dissociable from retrospective memory, and may reflect macrophage activation with axonal injury.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the impairment of prospective memory in persons with HIV may be dissociable and may reflect specific neurobiologic mechanisms of macrophages activation and axonal damage.
ProM impairment in persons with HIV infection may reflect macrophage-mediated axonal injury.
the impairment of prospective memory in persons with HIV infection is associated with the activation and injury of microglia, astrocytes, and neurons in the brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the neuropathogenesis and clinical manifestations of cognitive deficits associated with HIV-1 disease are likely to be complex and multifactorial, with distinct patterns of impairment in different cognitive domains.
the impairment in prospective memory is associated with markers of macrophage activity and axonal injury.
the mechanisms of HIV-1 neuropathology may be different for ProM than RM, and this has important implications for the development of treatments for cognitive dysfunction.
